FUB-Automation.title: FUB Automation — GTM Workflow Engine
FUB-Automation.stack: Java 21 · Spring Boot · React 19 · PostgreSQL · HMAC Webhooks
FUB-Automation.description: An event-driven GTM workflow automation engine for real-estate teams, built with a production-style architecture (controller → service → port → adapter → repository). It ingests signed Follow Up Boss webhook events, processes call outcomes asynchronously, and fires multi-step automations — follow-up tasks, lead qualification, and AI-driven first contact — so inbound leads never go cold. An operations admin layer adds live webhook ingestion, processed-call visibility, and replay for failed flows.
highlights: Event-driven workflow engine in Java 21 / Spring Boot that triggers multi-step automations the moment a CRM event lands — qualifying leads, creating follow-up tasks, and kicking off AI first contact.
HMAC-verified webhook ingestion using the inbox pattern with durable storage and dynamic trigger routing — zero event loss in production, fully decoupled from CRM sync latency.
Integrated an AI voice-calling service for automated first-touch qualification, capturing intent so agents enter each conversation with context instead of a cold call.
React 19 / TanStack Query operations console giving the team a single view of each lead with cross-linked calls, workflow runs, and activity history.

Careeros.title: CareerOS — AI Resume Intelligence
Careeros.stack: React · NestJS · FastAPI · PostgreSQL · pgvector · LangChain · RabbitMQ
Careeros.description: An AI-powered resume intelligence platform focused on practical hiring outcomes. It analyzes resumes for ATS compatibility, scoring quality, and improvement opportunities, then delivers structured feedback through a multi-service architecture — a React frontend, a NestJS BFF, and a Python FastAPI AI service — built for scalable analysis workflows and future automation layers.
highlights: Multi-service platform — React web, NestJS BFF, Python FastAPI AI service — for resume analysis and ATS scoring.
Production RAG pipeline over career data with LangChain, OpenAI embeddings, and pgvector — tuned chunking, semantic retrieval, and reranking for grounded, hallucination-resistant responses.
Offloaded heavy AI inference to RabbitMQ workers with idempotency keys, exponential backoff, and a dead-letter queue for predictable, exactly-once analysis.
Persisted analysis and scoring with PostgreSQL + Prisma and containerized the full stack with Docker for consistent local-to-prod workflows.

Corvanta.description: Corvanta is an autonomous HR operations platform designed for real estate brokerages, where onboarding velocity and compliance accuracy are critical. It automates core HR workflows such as new-agent onboarding, licensing/compliance checks, and operational follow-through while maintaining clear execution visibility. The product runs on a two-backend architecture: an orchestration service for workflow control and an intelligence service for specialized task execution.
highlights: Automates core HR workflows for real-estate brokerages — new-agent onboarding, licensing and compliance checks, and operational follow-through — with clear execution visibility.
Two-backend architecture: an orchestration service for workflow control and an intelligence service for specialized task execution.
Built on NestJS and Python services coordinated over RabbitMQ, with PostgreSQL persistence, containerized with Docker.

Spendora.title: Spendora — Local-First Expense Tracker
Spendora.description: A desktop-first personal expense tracker built with a React UI, a Tauri native shell, Rust local services, and a single-user SQLite database. Instead of relying on a remote backend, it runs an expense-api and a background expense-worker directly on your machine, with Tauri managing start/stop/status of both processes — designed for local-first performance, clear service lifecycle control, and a practical path for modular financial integrations.
highlights: Desktop-first architecture: a React UI runs inside a Tauri shell and controls local Rust services (expense-api, expense-worker) — no remote backend required.
Local-first persistence with SQLite and migration-driven schema initialization for reliable single-user operation.
Service lifecycle and health-check controls (start/stop/status) so the native shell manages the local API and worker processes cleanly.
